 EXCLUSIVE Pop Culture Pop Culture Jennifer Lopez Says She’s the ‘Happiest I’ve Been’ and Credits This 1 Change in Her Love Life
 In an extended conversation for TODAY’s podcast “Making Space,” Lopez opened up about her love life, becoming an empty nester and her new film, “The JLo Show.” Updated   Nov. 17, 2026, 12:55 PM EST / Source : TODAY Maura Hohman
 Assistant Managing Editor
 Jennifer Lopez Reveals Why She’s Finally in Her Happy Era 05:21 Share Add TODAY to Google After decades in the public eye and four divorces, Jennifer Lopez is no stranger to love, both feeling and talking about it. The complex emotion was a major theme in her lengthy sit-down with friend and former TODAY anchor Hoda Kotb, which aired in part on TODAY Nov. 17. The full extended version will be available as an episode of the “Making Space” podcast Nov. 18.
 “The thing for me is to be the love in the room,” Lopez, 57, told Hoda, 62. “To put love out into the world. To remind people that love exists. ... Love yourself and remember who you are. I’ve been on that journey, and once you remember who you are, you wanna remind others. ... I feel like for me, since (I was) very young, without knowing it, that’s been my purpose.”
 Hoda then revealed that one of the qualities she admires most about Lopez is her ability to fall in love. That prompted Hoda to share that she’s not sure if she’s ever been in love herself — “which gives me chills, and also makes me a little sad because it takes guts,” Hoda added.
 “It takes a fearlessness,” Lopez responded before explaining why she’s fine without having romantic love at the moment.
 “What you realize is what you’re searching for in another person is only up to you,” Lopez explained. “I have the ability to fall in love every day with my life, with the cup of coffee, with the bath, with the song I created that day.”
 “The only way you really learn these lessons is to make mistakes, to fail, to have things not work out the way you thought they were.”
 “It’s been kind of a two or three-year journey for me of really trying to understand myself, what my purpose is and what love is. And that for me has been a joy.”
 She said she’s since realized that love isn’t what makes you happy, but rather that you should make yourself happy.
 J.Lo and Hoda. Dana Samuel / TODAY “You have to really understand that that is in your hands, and it’s how you wake up every day. ... It’s how you choose to walk through the world, understanding your power, understanding everything about yourself that is only you uniquely and what you have to offer to the world. And I think for me, that made me look at romantic relationships differently, as well, because it’s not something that I need. It’s something that I would like.”
 “I have been the happiest I’ve been the past few years, where I’ve been single,” Lopez laughed. “But it took time to get there for me because I was such and I still am very much romantic.”
 Lopez is now able to see the positive in this mindset though, she told Hoda.
 “I used to beat that part of myself up. Like, that’s the reason I made these choices and these mistakes, and I’ve had these failures. ... I’ve been divorced several times. My kids didn’t have the things that I wanted them to have.”
 “And then you realize ... that romantic is the person who is able to go out into the world and create a life that I could have never dreamed of when I was growing up in the Bronx.”
 She said she sometimes struggled with how much of her personal life she made public. “I felt like it really overshadowed some of the work that I did and the things that I was really proud of ... And hurt me with opportunities as well, I think.”
 “Your star celebrity part of you becomes bigger than the work that you’re doing. And I would look at other people’s careers and go, ‘Why don’t they get this type of scrutiny? Why is it me?’” she chuckled.
 “I have to take responsibility in that I was very open about my life. I’ve never been kind of a guarded person in that way. I always wore my heart on my sleeve and was a very open book. And what I realize is that you have to have boundaries. That’s part of loving yourself. That’s part of it.”
 A recent, major change in Lopez’s life that’s allowed her more time to reflect is becoming an empty nester. Her twins, whom she shares with ex-husband Marc Anthony, recently left for college. But, like any other parent, she helped them decorate their rooms, sobbed and went on her way.
 “It was the first time I’ve lived alone in I don’t know how long, so that was really weird,” Lopez recalled. “Not having them down the hall does something to your heart. But I also realized I do enjoy my own company.”
 “I enjoy my space, and I never was like that. I was always so afraid of the quiet and of being alone. I think that’s what drove me to make some decisions that weren’t the best for me in my life. But I really feel at peace there in my house that I’ve built.”
 This major lifestyle change has helped inspire her in the recording studio, as well.
 “I’ve made some songs that really feel very me right now. They’re a little bit unapologetic. They’re very different than things that I’ve dared to write before,” Lopez said. “A lot of 20-year-olds ... make the pop music. I made the pop music when I was in my 20s, and I write for me and for people who experience what I’m experiencing. And it’s a different type of feeling. I think it’s important to do that, to have that voice out there, too.”
 Jennifer Lopez says she is in her "happy era." Dana Samuel / TODAY The rom-com star is also focused on another creative project: the Thanksgiving Day release of her concert film, “The JLo Show: Live From Las Vegas.” The title is a play on how public her life has been over the past few decades.
 “Yes, you’re watching ‘The JLo Show,’ me singing and dancing. But also, I started out watching ‘West Side Story’ on Thanksgiving in front of that TV, thinking about being an entertainer. I never thought that also my life, my personal life, would become the show and everything about me would be fair game,” Lopez explained.
 “I didn’t think about the fame side of this. I just thought, ‘I wanna sing and dance and act. That’s what I wanna do with my life.’ This other part that comes along with it. And so, it’s a real, interwoven piece about a mini-musical of my life.”
 So what’s next for the icon in her personal life? She told Hoda she’s setting boundaries and open to romantic partnership if it comes her way — but not just with anyone.
 “You get to a point where you have a certain standard, because if I’m on the floor or if I’m up here, it doesn’t matter,” Lopez said. “Is there somebody who can match who you are and the love that you’re capable of giving?”
 “Life is gonna take you in all those different directions, but having somebody who sees you and loves you in all of those iterations is really the goal.”
 The full “Making Space” episode with Jennifer Lopez comes out November 18th. Watch it on YouTube or listen on Spotify. Check out Season 9 of “Making Space” for conversations with Ina Garten, Mariska Hargitay, Sandra Bullock and more!
